transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News in Culver City, California,
I'm Dua Lee Saikowtao.
Black Friday shoppers filled malls across the country
from San Francisco to New York City.
In Atlanta, Kara Teising went shopping at Lenox Square,
which has more than 170 stores.
She said an AI chat bot helped her to find the best spots.
- It's Christmas gifts for the kids and clothes,
and I am normally very dubious of Black Friday.
Like, we tend to stay away from it,
but because we wanted the quality time together,
we decided to come.
I did use AI, I did use chat GPT
to kind of look and see which mall
had the biggest concentration of stores.
- The National Retail Federation
estimated spending both in stores and online
could jump over $1 trillion.
Online consumers already spent a record $7.1 billion
on Thanksgiving Day alone.
This is according to the Adobe Digital Insights Group,
which say this number is about a 12% increase from last year.
This year's Atlantic hurricane season
officially ends on Monday.
NPR's Debbie Elliott says 2026 has been one
of the quietest years on record for tropical activity.
The 2026 Atlantic hurricane season saw 10 named storms,
but only one of them reached hurricane strength.
That was the late forming Isaias
that struck the Florida panhandle
as a powerful category two hurricane in early October
and also caused damage in Alabama.
Cleanup is still underway along parts of the Gulf Coast.
Forecasters at Colorado State University
say only one hurricane is the fewest
in more than a century driven primarily
by a strong El Nino weather pattern.
That's when extremely warm Pacific ocean temperatures
dampen Atlantic hurricane activity.
Debbie Elliott, NPR News, Orange Beach, Alabama.
- A court in Kenya has convicted doomsday cult leader
Paul McKenzie of manslaughter
over the deaths of 123 of his followers.
He's already serving a 200 year sentence
for the murder of another 191 people.
Almost all of them children in the same mass killing.
Emmanuel Egunza reports from Nairobi.
- The High Court in Mombasa found that McKenzie
persuaded his followers to fast
until they died in Chakaola Forest between 2021 and 2023.
The court found that the plan was for children to die fast
than women than men with McKenzie himself going last.
McKenzie said he went to the forest to buy land
and that those who fasted did so on their free will.
McKenzie's wife was among 29 others convicted
while 60 were acquitted.
One of McKenzie's lawyers says he will appeal
this verdict after sentencing.
The deaths came to light in 2023
when hundreds of bodies were found in shallow graves
in one of the worst cult massacres of modern times.
- This is NPR.
Spaniards will head to the polls on Sunday
to decide if they want to keep Pedro Sanchez
as prime minister after eight years of leftist leadership
or choose Alberta Nunez-Feho
of the conservative Partido Popular Party
that's moving the country farther to the right.
But there's also the Vox Party led by Santiago Abascal.
His group could get enough votes this time
to maybe build a coalition government.
The snap election was called after protest
and unrest over high housing costs,
inflation and immigration.
And on the island of Taiwan,
polls are about to close in a closely watched local elections
by both Beijing and Washington,
including the Taipei City mayoral race.
The share of the world's population
that is not affiliated with any religion
is expected to drop in the coming decades.
And Piers Jason DeRose reports on the findings
of a report from Pew Research.
- About 2 billion people around the world
are religiously unaffiliated.
Pew says that number is expected to rise in most countries,
but researchers project that those increases
will be offset by an overall population drop
in one country, China.
The change isn't about people becoming religious,
rather a very large portion of the population there
is religiously unaffiliated.
In the coming decades,
China is expected to experience a dramatic population decrease
due to low birth rates.
Pew projects that the global population
of the religiously unaffiliated will drop from 24% to 17%
by the year 2070.
Jason DeRose, NPR News.
- And I'm Dua Halisa Kowtow, NPR News.

topics.text: Black Friday shoppers fill malls nationwide, with AI chatbots helping some pick shopping destinations
NRF estimates holiday spending could top $1 trillion; Adobe reports record Thanksgiving online sales
2026 Atlantic hurricane season ends with just one hurricane, the fewest in over a century, Debbie Elliott reports
Kenyan High Court convicts doomsday cult leader Paul McKenzie of manslaughter over 123 follower deaths
Spain heads to polls Sunday; Pedro Sanchez faces Alberto Nunez-Feijoo and the far-right Vox party
Taiwan polls close in local elections, including the closely watched Taipei City mayoral race
Pew Research projects unaffiliated share of world population falling from 24% to 17% by 2070, driven by China
